earnings.title: CHENIERE ENERGY, INC. NEWS RELEASE
highlights: Net income 1,2 was approximately $1.2 billion and $736 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to net income 1,2 of approximately $1.0 billion and $3.0 billion for the corresponding 2025 periods.

For the third quarter 2026, Cheniere’s Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.625 per common share, an increase of over 12% from the prior quarter, payable on November 17, 2026 to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 9, 2026.
Paying quarterly dividends of $0.555 and $1.665 per share of common stock, totaling approximately $114 million and $347 million, respectively,

quotes.text: We achieved key milestones across the Cheniere platform in the third quarter of 2026, highlighted by the substantial completion of the seventh and final train of the CCL Stage 3 Project, the export of our 5,000 th LNG cargo, and our continued commercial success in support of future brownfield growth at Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi.
quotes.by: Jack Fusco, Cheniere’s Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer

outlook: Cheniere Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Raises Full Year 2026 Financial Guidance, and Increases Quarterly Dividend by Over 12%

Raising full year 2026 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA 3 guidance from $7.90 billion - $8.40 billion to $8.75 billion - $9.25 billion and full year 2026 Distributable Cash Flow 3 guidance from $5.30 billion - $5.80 billion to $6.05 billion - $6.55 billion.

items.heading: An inability to source capital to supplement our available cash resources and existing credit facilities could cause us to have inadequate liquidity and could materially and adversely affect us.
items.group: Risks Relating to Our Financial Matters

items.heading: Our ability to generate cash is substantially dependent upon the performance by customers under long-term contracts that we have entered into, and we could be materially and adversely affected if any significant portion of our customers fails to perform its contractual obligations for any reason.

We and our subsidiaries may be restricted under the terms of our and their indebtedness from paying dividends or distributions under certain circumstances, which could materially and adversely affect our liquidity.

Restrictions in agreements governing us and our subsidiaries’ indebtedness may prevent us and our subsidiaries from engaging in certain beneficial transactions, which could materially and adversely affect us.
Our use of derivative instruments, including our IPM agreements, to manage risks could have a significant adverse or otherwise volatile effect on our earnings reported under GAAP and our liquidity.
Our ability to declare and pay dividends and repurchase shares is subject to certain considerations.
